newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes steady to firm, grades turn to Sept.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes steady to firm, grades turn to Sept.

text.p: Crude prices in the U.S. Gulf talked firm late Thursday, winding down a session dominated by the last stages of August grade business.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 10-15 cents stronger at $19.70-80 a barrel, with August/September rolls at minus 24-27 cents.

Cash dealers said Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James retained strength in September, talked late at a 21-22 cents premium. August LLS ranged around flat to 10 cents over the marker, but was only sporadically discussed.
Midland/WTI held a 25-35 cents discount to September WTI/Cushing, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at 35-45 cents under benchmark.
Sour crudes saw West Texas Sour/Midland talk at $1.65-70 under September WTI, with the price of Eugene Island set around $1.30-45 under marker.
Postings Plus for September closed around $1.93-95, working off a September/October spread of plus five to seven cents.

Market talk quieted on the Iraqi front, with the situation at status quo. U.N. officials were still reviewing Baghdad's aid distribution plan, and waiting for further details to arrive by the weekend when annexes to the main text are to arrive in New York.
Western diplomats said Iraq would not be allowed to change oil sales deadlines spelled out in the "oil-for-food" accord, setting the stage for a crush of Iraqi oil exports in August.
Completion of the U.N. review was still pegged for end of the July, diplomats and U.N. officials said.
Traders said outright price gains were mainly due to strong gasoline markets, which saw heavy refiner buying.
